# Droid Vault 4.0.0

## New in this release

- **The app is no longer blue.** The accent is now a muted plum instead of a
  fully saturated periwinkle, and the backgrounds, cards and surfaces are warm
  greys rather than blue-tinted ones.

- **You can pick the app's colour.** Settings → Theme → Accent colour opens the
  full Material palette — nineteen colour families and every shade of each —
  plus a field for a colour of your own. Three contrast steps come with it,
  from soft to punchy. Your colour applies straight away, and a Reset puts
  Droid Vault's own plum back.

- **Buttons are quieter.** A filled action used to be a bright block of colour;
  it is now a soft plate in the accent's own colour. The action still reads as
  the action — it just stops shouting.

- **The button that deletes now looks like the button that deletes.** Every
  destructive confirmation wears the error colour, so the only saturated thing
  on a confirmation screen is the thing that destroys.

- **A configuration's dry run no longer lists every app it does not cover.** It
  ends with one sentence and a number instead of hundreds of identical rows.

- **A configuration that only handles device data shows that, and nothing else.**
  Its dry run used to be a list of every app on the phone under a "0 apps"
  heading, and the button that starts the backup was greyed out. It now lists
  the device data it handles, and the button works.

- **A configuration can leave out individual apps.** Open its dry run and switch
  an app off, and that configuration will not touch it — even though a label
  covers it. The apps you switch off are listed separately, and the choice is
  saved.

- **A configuration's excluded apps can be reset.** The card says how many apps
  a configuration leaves alone, and a Reset beside it puts them all back in one
  tap.

- **The folder picker now opens at your vault folder.** Choosing a new location
  for your backups started at the top of storage, so you had to scroll down to
  DroidVault every time. It now opens where your backups already are.

## Fixed in this release

- **The restoration page now appears whenever a restore is running.** It used to
  appear only on the screen that started the run, so rotating the phone or
  reopening the app during a restore left it hidden until the restore ended.

- **A restored app goes back into the launcher as soon as its own data is
  back.** It used to stay hidden until every other app had been restored, so the
  app drawer filled in all at once at the end.

- **A device item that could not be restored now says so.** The Wi-Fi, wallpaper
  and Bluetooth restores were discarding the engine's answer, so a restore that
  restored nothing was recorded as a success.

- **A message that is already on the phone is no longer written again.** A
  message whose archived text ended in a line break was treated as a different
  message, so every restore added another copy of it and then reported it as one
  that could not be written.

- **The notification says what the run is doing, and always ends with a
  result.** It used to read "Restore started" for the whole run, could not be
  swiped away, and sometimes stayed there after the run was over.

- **The time-left figure no longer grows while the run is working.** It was an
  average over the whole run, so a part that was busy for a while made the
  estimate climb. It is also measured from the data actually being written now,
  so a skipped part no longer makes a run look nearly finished.

- **A restore starts checking only the backups it is about to restore.** The
  check before a restore read every backup in the vault, which for an eight-app
  restore meant reading fifteen gigabytes to vouch for one — about 85 seconds
  of waiting, with nothing on screen to say why. It now reads the backups in
  the plan, on four cores, and the run screen appears straight away and says
  what it is doing.

- **The dry-run preview reads in the reading colour.** Its notes, headings and
  component lists were painted in the link colour, so they looked like links.

- **The completed screen no longer carries a bright bar under its title**, and
  the row of finished app icons is centred instead of hanging off the left edge.

## Upgrading

Your backup folder is untouched. Install over your existing copy — your
settings, labels, app assignments, configurations and scheduled jobs are kept.

This replaces 3.0.2 directly.

## Download

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `arm64-v8a-release.apk` | Almost all phones from 2017 onward |
| `armeabi-v7a-release.apk` | Older 32-bit phones |

Not sure? Take the 64-bit one.

**Needs** a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) and Android 10+.

Please keep a second backup somewhere else.
